Definition: from G4835; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate:--have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
BiblicalUsage: We do not have a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one tempted in all points as we are, yet without sin, and the Hebrews had compassion on Paul in his bonds and took joyfully the spoiling of their goods. Christ feels with us from heaven, and His people feel with one another on earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that my High Priest truly feels what I feel, and I believe His sympathy is the ground of my confidence to come boldly to Him.
